# aontu

> aontu is a JSON-superset unification language and validation gate for
> AI-agent ground truth. One document can carry data, the schema that
> constrains it, and the defaults that fill it in; a single operation —
> unification — combines them or reports exactly where they conflict,
> with two-sited findings and stable error codes. The toolchain's verbs
> serve the agent loop: `vet` validates data against a schema, `get` and
> `why` query a document and explain a value's provenance, `subsume` and
> `breaking` gate schema evolution, `hash` pins what a document means,
> `set` repairs a value in place, `relations` checks declared entity
> graphs, `reaches` answers whether one entity reaches another at any
> remove, `view` draws a model as text (tree, matrix, graph, layers,
> sets, the meet ladder, the subsumption poset, the key document and
> the value lattice), `fmt` writes the one agreed form,
> `jsonschema` exports the model as JSON Schema and reports
> what that export cannot carry, `help` serves the language itself
> from inside the binary, `explain` answers what one error code
> means and `init` writes a working model, its data and a check script
> to start from, and an MCP server exposes the same
> contracts over stdio. Two
> implementations (TypeScript, canonical, npm `aontu`; a Go port) are
> kept in parity by one shared conformance suite, under a written trust
> contract (hermeticity, termination, determinism, sandboxing).

## Docs

- [Documentation home](docs/index.md): the map of the documentation and
  a 30-second taste of the language
- [Tutorials](docs/tutorial.md): four tutorials, each building one
  thing with the output of every step shown — a config that checks
  itself ([docs/tutorial-config.md](docs/tutorial-config.md):
  unification, types, exact numbers, defaults, references, templates,
  vet), the graph layer
  ([docs/tutorial-graph.md](docs/tutorial-graph.md): identity across
  two views, declared relations, reachability, recursive schemas),
  sharing a model as a package
  ([docs/tutorial-package.md](docs/tutorial-package.md): `pkg.aontu`,
  `aontu publish`, the lockfile pins, the vendor tree, the publish
  gate) and generating files from a model
  ([docs/tutorial-generate.md](docs/tutorial-generate.md): `emit`,
  `each`, and the component tree of project, folder, file and line
  nodes)
- [Language reference](docs/reference-language.md): every construct and
  rule — the exhaustive, dry source of truth for the language
- [Generation reference](docs/reference-generation.md): the component
  tree, every node and its props, the children each admits, and what
  `aontu render` and `aontu trace` do with a tree
- [Functions reference](docs/reference-functions.md): the call surface
  of all 64 built-ins, as one table and as slices through it: arity,
  argument modes, accepted kinds, result words
- [Error reference](docs/reference-errors.md): every registered error
  code, by class, with what raises it and what a report carries
- [API reference](docs/reference-api.md): the CLI verbs with flags and
  exit codes, the TypeScript and Go APIs, and the MCP server
- [Trust contract](docs/trust.md): the guarantees a host may rely on
  when evaluating a document, and exactly where each is conditional

## Agent-facing

- [aontu skill](docs/skill/SKILL.md): a teaching pack for agents — the
  task-to-verb index, the grammar card, a worked example ladder, and
  the error-code index. It also ships INSIDE the command: `aontu help`
  lists the topics and `aontu help language` prints the grammar card,
  so an agent with the binary and no network still has it, and
  `aontu init` writes a known-good document to edit rather than invent
- [Grammars](grammar/): `aontu.abnf`, the notation a person reads, and
  `aontu.gbnf`, `aontu.lark` and `aontu.tmLanguage.json` — the emission
  surface for constrained decoding of canonical aontu, and the
  highlighting grammar

## Conformance and use cases

- [Shared spec suite](test/spec/): the conformance corpus — 3k+
  language-agnostic cases both implementations must satisfy; a third
  implementation claims conformance by passing it
- [Use cases](use-cases/): eighteen enterprise-shaped systems built as
  real aontu documents, each with a `check.sh` that drives the CLI and
  asserts every outcome

## Contributing

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): the contributor and agent guide — layout,
  build/test, the shared-spec workflow, and the parity probe
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): the security policy — confinement
  escapes, budget bypasses and hermeticity breaks are in scope
